R2_comment: Can be burned as fuel asks physical possibility rather than customary use; animal tissue is combustible too, so the categorical cat=no is not secure. Better: Is it commonly burned in household stoves for heat? (wood yes, cat no).
Accept a generic usual cooking method, not a claim that every pasta dish is boiled.
Boxed dried pasta is made from dough even after drying; the drafter's manufacturing distinction does not change the answer.
Accept ordinary anatomical tail, rather than a figurative rear section.
Pizzicato does not negate the generic fact that violin is played with a bow.
The supplied yes is correct for the ordinary adult frog, but the drafter explicitly relies on life stage. Better: In its adult form, does it normally eat insects? (violin no, frog yes).
Yes fits a whole unpeeled egg, but egg as a food also ordinarily means a peeled or cooked serving with no shell. Better: In its intact uncooked form, is it enclosed by a shell? (egg yes, lion no).
The animals family fixes mouse to the animal sense; no computer-sense ambiguity remains.

Quarrying is an ordinary way of digging/extracting rock from the ground, consistent with the drafter note.

Yes is correct for dairy cheese, but unqualified cheese can include plant-based varieties in ordinary contemporary use. Better: Is it traditionally produced by curdling milk? (cheese yes, screw no).
Accept edible as food, not the mere possibility of swallowing an inedible object.

The intended contrast is correct for ripe flesh, but hardness depends on ripeness and whether skin or stone is included. Better: Is its ripe flesh normally eaten? (mango yes, marble no; reverse the supplied answer polarity).

Travel is understood as the intended transport function, not being carried as cargo.

Yes is correct for a crewed submarine, but the note selects a narrower sense not declared in concepts.json; uncrewed forms exist. Better: Is it designed to travel beneath the water surface? (submarine yes, trumpet no).
The no assumes a full-size crewed submarine; small uncrewed forms can be smaller than a person. Better: Is it normally played by a musician? (submarine no, trumpet yes).

Referees use signal whistles, while all twelve bank clues describe the melodic tin-whistle subtype. The word-level yes is defensible but the sense switches across tasks. Better: Does blowing into it normally produce a musical tone? (whistle yes, steel no), with the whistle sense declared consistently.

Yes assumes the ordinary one-piece threaded fastener; expansion-bolt assemblies and door-bolt mechanisms create a construction/word-sense dependency. Better: Is it commonly tightened with a nut to join parts? (bicycle no, bolt yes).

Yes fits the standard pedal bicycle, but balance bikes are a familiar pedal-free variety: https://striderbikes.com/faq/ . Better: Does it normally have two wheels arranged one behind the other? (bicycle yes, bolt no).

Yes assumes combustion power or treats motor and engine as synonyms; electric tractors use batteries and motors. Manufacturer evidence: https://www.monarchtractor.com/blog/cost-to-charge-ev . Better: Does it have a powered drive system for moving over ground? (needle no, tractor yes).

Yes fits sharp sewing/hypodermic varieties, but blunt tapestry and darning needles are ordinary alternatives. Better: Is it a slender implement used to pass thread through fabric? (needle yes, tractor no), explicitly selecting the sewing sense.
Accept the general sewing use; this does not claim that every specialized needle is used for sewing.
